R1M4_common: On this balanced set every model is far less consistent on computed-metallic compositions (PCR 0.21-0.40) than on gapped ones (0.84-0.96), a shared default towards calling compositions non-metallic that the imbalanced sample hid.
R2W4_common: On this set of 90 materials per DFT type (45 per reference class; for stability, 34 near-hull draws are not scored under the corrected oracle, leaving 56; eight models), none of the stated comparisons is significant when restricted to the DFT constraint types: GPT-5.6-Terra vs GPT-4o +0.021 (95% CI -0.042 to 0.085), Claude Opus 4.6 vs Claude Sonnet 4.5 +0.021 (-0.030 to 0.072), GPT-5.6-Sol vs GPT-5.6-Terra +0.030 (-0.013 to 0.072); 3 of 28 pairs differ after Holm correction, all with Gemini 2.5 Flash Lite lower (Supplementary Table S6). The GPT-5.6-Terra vs GPT-4o difference in the main evaluation therefore comes from the image constraint types, chiefly spectra, and we say so. The locally run Qwen2.5-VL-7B was evaluated on CPU in single precision for this set.
R1M2_xrd: For diffraction, the opXRD patterns are sampled every 0.013 degrees (median) and the FWHM of the strongest peak has a median of 0.12 degrees (IQR 0.06-0.21), so the 0.5 degree tolerance is about four times a typical peak width; it is set instead by what can be read from the plot shown to the model (a median 0.14 degrees per pixel), so it corresponds to three to four pixels, while the 0.1 degree accuracy criterion is close to one pixel and to a typical peak width.
R1M3_xrd: On diffraction (n=245), accuracy rises from 22.9% to 28.6%: 14 items become accurate and none ceases to be (p=0.0001); of the 79 revised items, 41 cleared the oracle, 14 by moving to the accurate value and 27 to an admissible but inexact value, and 38 remained flagged.
ED1_service: The authors carried out the language revision themselves: every revised passage was rewritten for clarity, long sentences were split, and internal jargon and project-specific labels were removed (see also Reviewer 2, weakness 1).
R1M2_silent: The oracles rarely miss genuine violations on real responses: the miss rate is 1/30 for diffraction, 2/30 for microscopy, 1/30 for spectra and 0/30, 0/30 and 0/29 for stability, metallicity and magnetism (Wilson 95% upper bounds 11-21%), which corresponds to an implied recall of 0.97, 0.81, 0.995 and 1.00, 1.00, 1.00 (Supplementary Table S8). Microscopy, whose oracle checks only the field of view, is the least complete, and we say so.
R2W3_adjudication: Both annotators then adjudicated together the 24 subsampled cases on which they disagreed (9 diffraction, 2 microscopy, 11 spectra, 2 magnetism). The consensus sided with the second annotator in all 22 diffraction, spectrum and magnetism disputes and with the first annotator in both microscopy disputes. Weighted back by stratum, consensus precision is 0.60 [0.44, 0.75] for diffraction, 0.89 [0.82, 0.94] for microscopy, 0.61 [0.44, 0.76] for spectra, 1.00 [0.84, 1.00] for stability, 0.95 [0.87, 0.97] for metallicity and 0.91 [0.80, 0.97] for magnetism. Table 1 now reports this consensus precision beside the single-annotator value, and the text states plainly that for diffraction and spectra roughly four in ten fired cases are boundary readings that both annotators agree are not violations, so the PCR of these two families understates the true rate more than the single-annotator audit suggested.
